question: Should experiment-gated Claw lifecycle ownership diagnostics become a core doctor surface once the prerequisite stack and non-mutating read contract are proven?
rationale: The implementation is technically separable, but an open RFC and stacked unmerged ownership model do not establish whether OpenClaw should permanently own this lifecycle feature in core.

options.title: Sponsor after proof
options.body: Accept the core direction after the prerequisite lands, WAL-sidecar behavior is resolved, and inspectable real behavior proof is added.

options.title: Evaluate the full stack
options.body: Keep this draft unlanded until maintainers review the RFC and all dependent Claws lifecycle slices together.

options.title: Decline core ownership
options.body: Close the stack if Claw package lifecycle ownership should not become an OpenClaw core capability.

recommendation.title: Sponsor after proof
recommendation.body: Accept the core direction after the prerequisite lands, WAL-sidecar behavior is resolved, and inspectable real behavior proof is added.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent shared-state and doctor architecture work makes this the strongest available owner for both the persistence contract and core-boundary decision.
